questions.stem: Which statement about workers compensation in the United States is most accurate?
options: One identical federal benefit schedule applies everywhere
Benefits and procedures are primarily established by state law and vary by jurisdiction
Employers may define benefits independently of law
Only OSHA decides compensability
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Workers compensation is largely state-based, so a safety professional should verify the law and claims process for the applicable jurisdiction.
incorrectOptionExplanations: State systems differ in coverage, benefits, procedures, and exceptions.
Employers and insurers operate within applicable legal requirements.
OSHA recordability and workers compensation compensability are separate determinations.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 23, current workers compensation laws, pp. 538-545

questions.stem: A claim is accepted for workers compensation but does not meet OSHA recording criteria. What is the correct conclusion?
options: Every accepted claim must be on the OSHA 300 Log
No accepted claim can be recordable
Compensability and OSHA recordability are separate decisions under different rules
The insurer decides OSHA recordability
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A case may be compensable but not recordable, recordable but disputed for compensation, or both, depending on the governing criteria.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Workers compensation acceptance does not automatically satisfy federal recordkeeping criteria.
Many compensable cases may also be recordable, but not all.
The employer is responsible for applying OSHA recordkeeping requirements.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapters 3 and 23, recordability and compensability, pp. 44-54 and 538-545

questions.stem: What does an experience modification factor generally compare?
options: Employee age with retirement eligibility
OSHA penalties with annual revenue
Training hours with production hours only
An employer loss experience with expected losses for comparable operations
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: The experience factor adjusts premium based on actual loss experience relative to expected experience, subject to the rating system rules.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Age and retirement status do not define the insurance experience factor.
Regulatory penalties are not the basis of the factor.
Training and production hours may be useful metrics but are not the expected-loss comparison.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 23, premiums and experience modification rates, pp. 541-542

options: Use medically supported functional restrictions, meaningful transitional work, communication, and periodic review
Return every employee to full duty immediately
Create punitive tasks to discourage claims
Keep the employee off work until completely symptom-free regardless of capability
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A coordinated program matches safe productive work to current capability and adjusts as recovery progresses.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Full duty without regard to restrictions can cause reinjury and violate medical limits.
Punitive work damages trust and is not legitimate rehabilitation.
Appropriate transitional work may support recovery and function when medically permitted.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 23, case management and return-to-work programs, pp. 543-545

questions.stem: Why is prompt injury reporting valuable beyond administrative compliance?
options: It guarantees that every claim will be denied
It supports timely care, evidence preservation, investigation, claim management, and early return-to-work planning
It eliminates the need for investigation
It converts every first-aid case into lost time
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Early information allows appropriate treatment and coordinated decisions while facts are still available.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Prompt reporting should support fair and accurate handling, not predetermined denial.
Early notice improves rather than replaces investigation.
Reporting does not change the medical or recordkeeping classification by itself.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 23, reporting injuries and claims and prompt reporting, pp. 543-544

questions.stem: What is subrogation in a workers compensation context?
options: The employee waives all medical treatment
OSHA transfers a citation to the insurer
The insurer or employer seeks recovery from a responsible third party after paying benefits
The employer deletes the injury from its records
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Subrogation prevents a responsible third party from escaping liability and can recover costs paid under the compensation system.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Subrogation concerns third-party recovery, not waiver of care.
OSHA citations are not transferred through insurance subrogation.
Claims recovery does not change accurate OSHA recordkeeping duties.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 23, waiver of subrogation and insurance concepts, pp. 541-543
